paragraphs: Friend, this passage is about a man who got exactly what he fought for and still lost something huge. David's men won the battle, and the runners came with news of victory. But David only asked one thing: "Is the young man Absalom all right?" (2 Samuel 18:29, 32). A win on the field can't fix a wound in the heart, and David's cry, "O my son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom!" shows how deep that wound went (2 Samuel 18:33).

Now here's the part that matters for you. Grief is real, and I think David's tears show a father's love that didn't quit even when his son turned on him. But Joab tells him the people who stood by him were being left out in the cold, and that day's victory "was turned into mourning for all the people" (2 Samuel 19:2). Our sorrow is real, but it can leave the people beside us standing there quietly with nobody looking their way.

So the lesson is to feel it AND still show up. David got up and sat in the gate, and the people came before him (2 Samuel 19:8). I think that took everything he had. When you're hurting, friend, let yourself hurt, and then go out to the people who stayed with you. Don't pack up the tears, just make room for them to stand at the gate with you.
